mite.configuration.title: MITE: Gameplay settings
mite.config.gameplay.tooltip: Configure growth multipliers, melee reach, trial structures and advanced enchantment overrides.
mite.config.registry_enchantments.toolti: Edit enchantment level limits and random acquisition probabilities from the title screen. Entering a world adds mod and data pack enchantments while keeping your edits.
mite.config.enter_world: The default catalog is editable from the title screen. Entering a world refreshes registry metadata and adds new enchantments while retaining overrides.
mite.config.server_owned: Multiplayer uses server settings. Saving requires OP permission and a server that supports online editing.
mite.config.remote.scope: OP saves apply to the server and sync to all players. Ores and trials affect new chunks.
mite.config.remote.no_permission: Save rejected: OP permission (level 2 or higher) is required.
mite.config.remote.denied: Saving requires OP permission and a server that supports online editing.
mite.config.remote.invalid: Invalid configuration. The server did not apply these changes. Check the value ranges.
mite.config.remote.save_failed: The server could not save the configuration. Check the server log.
mite.config.remote.send_failed: Could not send the configuration. Check your connection and retry.
mite.config.remote.timeout: The server has not confirmed this save. Check the current settings before retrying.
mite.config.remote.disconnected: Disconnected before the save could be confirmed.
mite.config.async_pathfinding.tooltip: Spread supported hostile melee path searches across server ticks to reduce tick spikes. Applies on save.
mite.config.scope: Saves apply live; ores and trials affect new chunks. Configure enchantments from the title screen; worlds add new entries. Multiplayer uses server settings.
mite.config.scope_compact: Saves apply live; ores and trials affect new chunks. Multiplayer uses server settings.
mite.config.export.tooltip: Export all saved local gameplay settings. If ITE is installed, include its common configs so the whole package can be placed in the server's config folder. Save changes on each settings page first.
mite.config.export.remote: Currently viewing server settings. Disconnect before exporting your local configuration.
mite.config.export.saved: The complete local gameplay configuration was exported to this folder:
mite.config.export.install: Install on a server: stop the server, copy all TOML files listed above into its config folder, replace matching files, then start the server. Install ITE on the server when using its configuration.
mite.config.export.saved_only: Includes all saved gameplay settings. When ITE is installed, its common configs, including ITE monster spawn rates, are discovered and exported too. Unsaved drafts are excluded. Each export creates a separate copy.
mite.config.export.failure_hint: Configuration could not be exported. Check the reason below and try again. Details were recorded in the game log.
mite.config.search_all.tooltip: Search MITE and ITE setting names, descriptions, categories or keys. Separate words with spaces; clear to return to categories.
mite.config.async_pathfinding.tooltip: Spread supported hostile path searches across background workers to reduce server tick spikes. Path decisions may be delayed.
mite.config.ai_load_reduction.tooltip: Stagger expensive animal food/water scans and hostile path searches to reduce server load. Some AI decisions may be delayed.
mite.config.maximum.tooltip: Original maximum: %s. Untouched values keep original rules. Enter 1–255 for an explicit cap, or 0 to clear it. Reset clears the cap and enables the enchantment.
mite.config.enchantment_chance.tooltip: Candidate participation probability for random enchanting: 0–100, decimals allowed. 100%% preserves default participation; 0%% excludes this enchantment from random selection. Final results still depend on the current enchanting path's weights, level requirements and compatibility; 100%% does not guarantee selection. Only random acquisition is affected; existing enchantment effects remain active.
mite.config.enchantment_reset.tooltip: Restore the bundled default level cap, enabled state and random participation probability. Apply with Save.
mite.config.invalid_enchantment_entries: %s invalid inputs: cap must be an integer from 0–255; probability must be a finite number from 0–100.
mite.config.enchantment_automatic: Original rules apply; the displayed default is not an override.
mite.config.enchantment_override: Explicit cap; catalog refreshes preserve this value.
mite.config.enchantment_offline: Source: bundled defaults or cached registry; refreshed when entering a world.
mite.config.enchantment_cached: Not registered in this world; cached metadata and your settings are retained.
mite.config.enchantment_unresolved: Registry metadata has not been discovered. Original maximum unknown; 0 keeps original rules.
mite.config.enchantment_enable_hint: Currently disabled. Click to enable, then save to apply.
mite.config.enchantment_disable_hint: Currently enabled. Click to disable, then save to apply.
mite.config.enchantment_hint: Cap 0 clears override; chance 100%% preserves default participation, 0%% excludes random acquisition. Hover for details.
mite.config.underworld_ores.tooltip: Derived from the underworld generator rules. 1 = default amount; 0 = disabled. Only affects new chunks.
mite.config.monster_spawning.tooltip: Set each monster's natural spawn weight directly. A higher weight increases its selection chance within the same pool. ITE entities are configured in ITE settings. Saved changes apply immediately.
mite.config.natural_spawn_rates.tooltip: Format namespace:entity=multiplier, range 0–100. 1 preserves original weights; 0 disables natural spawning. The dedicated page displays percentages. Unloaded entity IDs are retained.
mite.config.natural_spawn_weights.toolti: Override existing natural pool base weights by entity ID: namespace:entity=number, decimals allowed, range 0–1000000. Omitted entities retain each pool's native weight, followed by the spawn-rate multiplier.
mite.config.monster_spawn_percent.toolti: 100% keeps the weight, 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, and 0% disables natural spawning of this final species. Range 0–10000%. When an explicit pool weight is set, this multiplier applies afterward. Actual selection also depends on other candidates and existing spawn conditions.
mite.config.monster_spawn_weight.tooltip: Set this monster's natural spawn weight directly: 0–1000000, including decimals such as 2.5 or 0.25. Higher weights increase selection chances within the same pool. Blank restores each pool's native value. Editing or resetting this entry replaces its legacy multiplier. 0 disables the whole candidate family, including transformed variants. This is not a percentage and does not create a natural spawn entry.
mite.config.monster_spawn_weight_unavail: No independent natural pool entry is currently identified. Weights do not create natural entries for bosses or other creatures without one. Existing or unknown ID settings are retained and can be removed with Reset.
mite.config.monster_spawn_weight_hint: Blank inherits native weights; 0 disables the candidate family. Higher weights increase relative spawn chances. Saved changes apply immediately.
mite.config.monster_spawn_reset.tooltip: Restore this monster's bundled default spawn weight and multiplier; unspecified weights use the native value.
mite.config.monster_spawn_weight_invalid: Invalid draft, possibly on another page: spawn weights must be blank or finite numbers 0–1000000; decimals are allowed.
mite.config.monster_spawn_conditional: Weight follows existing conditions or variant rules
mite.config.monster_spawn_hint: 100% keeps the current weight; 0% disables this final species. Multipliers also adjust conditional variants. Caps and existing spawn conditions still apply.
mite.config.monster_spawn_details: Edit existing natural pool weights in the Overworld, Nether, End and underworld. Date, depth, light, pack and population rules still apply. Existing mobs, spawners, dungeons, spawn eggs and commands are unaffected. Unknown IDs are retained.
mite.config.monster_spawn_save_hint: Save valid spawn weights across every page; subsequent natural spawns use them immediately.
mite.config.monster_spawn_invalid: Invalid legacy multiplier: enter finite percentages 0–10000 before saving.
mite.config.monsters.tooltip: Adjust calendar-based health growth. Monster damage does not grow with the date.
mite.config.growth_multiplier.tooltip: Multiplies the formula's rate variable. 1 keeps defaults. With the default formula, 0 disables growth; custom formulas that ignore rate are unaffected.
mite.config.health_growth_multiplier.too: Multiplied by overall growth and then into the health formula's rate variable. Custom formulas that ignore rate are unaffected.
mite.config.damage_growth_multiplier.too: Inactive legacy compatibility value. Monster damage does not grow with the date.
mite.config.combat.tooltip: Adjust survival melee reach and Better Combat mob compatibility with matching client and server settings.
mite.config.better_combat_mobs.tooltip: Disabled by default: mobs use their original attacks. Enable to give armed hostile mobs Better Combat windups, combos, cooldowns and animations. Requires Better Combat. Player compatibility is unaffected.
mite.config.weapon_reach_multiplier.tool: MITE and Simply Swords select separate family ranges according to Better Combat availability, then apply this multiplier and the fixed reduction. Default multiplier 1.
mite.config.weapon_reach_reduction.toolt: Subtract from multiplied melee reach, with a minimum of 0. Default 0. This setting does not change damage.
mite.config.height_reach_penalty.tooltip: Use MITE target-height reach adjustments. Disable to ignore target height for melee reach. Also applies to Better Combat attacks.
mite.config.structures.tooltip: Controls new structure starts. Existing buildings remain. Disabled types are also excluded from locate.
mite.config.underworld_trials.tooltip: Allow new underworld trial structure starts. Existing structures remain.
mite.config.overworld_trials.tooltip: Allow new overworld trial chamber starts. Existing structures remain.
mite.config.enchantments.tooltip: Use the enchantment settings from the title screen for convenient editing. These lists contain explicit overrides, preserved when the default catalog refreshes.
mite.config.disabled_enchantments.toolti: Use namespace:id. Blocks acquisition and effects while retaining saved enchantment data for re-enabling.
mite.config.enchantment_max_levels.toolt: Format namespace:id=level, range 1–255. Only changed entries are saved; unknown IDs are retained.
mite.config.enchantment_chances.tooltip: Format namespace:id=percent, range 0–100; decimals allowed, default 100. Candidate participation only: 100%% preserves default participation, 0%% excludes random acquisition. The current enchanting path's weights, levels and compatibility still decide selection. Existing enchantment effects are unaffected; unknown IDs are retained.
mite.config.ore.gravel.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.coal.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.emerald.tooltip: Singleton attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.copper.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.silver.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.gold.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.iron.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.mithril.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.adamantium.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.redstone.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.diamond.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.lapis.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore.infested.tooltip: Vein attempt multiplier: 1 = default, 0 = disabled. Supports fractions; new chunks only.
mite.config.ore_multiplier.tooltip: Candidate vein attempts per chunk × multiplier. 1 = original multiplier, 2 = double, 0.5 = half, 0 = disabled. Fractional candidates use random rounding. Probability filtering is unchanged; affects new chunks only.
mite.config.monster_formulas.tooltip: Edit and preview health growth bases and formulas, and set a fixed innate attack base.
mite.config.health_base.tooltip: All monsters share this first-period growth reference. 0 uses the default 20. Each entity retains its native spawn health, including 6 for ordinary skeletons. Range 0–1024. Later periods reference actual settled health.
mite.config.damage_base: Fixed innate attack base (0 = entity default)
mite.config.damage_base.tooltip: 0 preserves each entity's innate attack; range 0–2048. This base is independent of the world date, and weapon bonuses are added separately.
mite.config.skeleton_reference.tooltip: Retained for existing settings. All monsters now use the shared first-period health reference.
mite.config.health_daily_percent.tooltip: Default 0.5 adds 0.5% of the period's reference health per day. Formula rate = this value / 100 × overall multiplier × health multiplier. Range 0–100.
mite.config.damage_daily_percent.tooltip: Default 0.25 adds 0.25% of the period's attack per day. Formula rate = this value / 100 × overall multiplier × damage multiplier. Range 0–100.
mite.config.health_formula.tooltip: Current health = this expression. Default: base + reference * rate * days. The base comes from blood-moon rebasing, rather than always being the initial health. Up to 512 characters; validation is required.
mite.config.damage_formula.tooltip: Current innate attack = this expression. Default: base + reference * rate * days. The base comes from the blood-moon formula. Weapon attributes are added separately. Up to 512 characters; validation is required.
mite.config.health_blood_moon_formula: Blood moon: next health base formula (editable)
mite.config.health_blood_moon_formula.to: After each blood moon, evaluate this with the previous base, reference and full period days, then set reference = base. Default: base + reference * rate * days. An empty TOML value inherits the within-period formula; this page shows the resolved expression.
mite.config.damage_blood_moon_formula: Blood moon: next attack base formula (editable)
mite.config.damage_blood_moon_formula.to: After each blood moon, evaluate the next innate attack base with the previous period's inputs, then set reference = base. Default: base + reference * rate * days. An empty TOML value inherits the within-period formula; this page shows the resolved expression.
mite.config.growth_baseline_hint: Default: +0.5% health daily. Health calculation includes blood-moon rebasing and within-period growth. Both editable expressions below are executed. Blue moons do not rebase. Scroll to see the complete form.
mite.config.fixed_damage_hint: Monster damage no longer grows with the world date. This page only sets a fixed innate melee attack base; arrows, spells and other attacks retain their own base damage.
mite.config.health_recurrence_initial: The first base[0] and initial use native entity health. All monsters share a default reference[0] of 20, adding 20 × 0.5% = 0.1 health daily.
mite.config.damage_recurrence_initial: Initially: base[0] = reference[0] = initial (innate attack, excluding weapons).
mite.config.growth_recurrence_blood: After a blood moon: base[n+1] = blood-moon formula(base[n], initial, reference[n], rate, full period days, day, blood_moons=n); reference[n+1] = base[n+1]. The expression below computes this new base.
mite.config.growth_recurrence_period: Current attribute = within-period formula(base[n], initial, reference[n], rate, days, day, blood_moons=n). Days restart after each blood-moon settlement; the base is the result of the blood-moon recurrence above.
mite.config.growth_recurrence_calendar: Settle after days 32, 64, 96, 160, etc. Day 128 and its multiples are blue moons and skip settlement. Blood-moon days are normally 32, or 64 across a blue moon; its day variable is the date following that blood moon.
mite.config.growth_variables: Both expressions share: base = previous/current period base; initial = initial base; reference = that period's reference; rate = daily fractional rate; days = full elapsed days of that period; day = evaluation date; blood_moons = settlements completed before this execution, excluding blue moons.
mite.config.growth_functions: Operators: + - * / % ^ and parentheses (^ is power). Functions: abs, sqrt, log, exp, floor, ceil, min, max, pow, clamp. Example: base * pow(1 + rate, days).
mite.config.growth_preview_heading: Execution preview (sample entity values, not saved)
mite.config.health_native.tooltip: Tests native spawn health. Enter 6 for an ordinary skeleton. Greater than 0 through 1024.
mite.config.damage_native.tooltip: Original innate attack for preview, range 0–2048, excluding weapons. Does not modify any entity.
mite.config.preview_day.tooltip: Initially uses the world's current date. Enter a positive integer to test another date. Actual growth uses the world's highest historical date and never reverses when time is set back.
mite.config.growth_preview_context: Inputs: base=%s, reference=%s, days=%s, blood_moons=%s, day=%s; additional rate multiplier=%s.
mite.config.growth_preview_initial: Shared initial = %s, taken from native entity health.
mite.config.growth_preview_rate: Effective daily fractional rate = %s (includes overall and attribute multipliers).
mite.config.growth_preview_no_blood: No settled blood moons: base = initial; reference uses the initial-period rule.
mite.config.growth_preview_blood: Latest blood-moon settlement (#%s, day=%s): new base = %s
mite.config.growth_preview_blood_inputs: Settlement inputs: base=%s, reference=%s, days=%s, blood_moons=%s; new base = reference = %s.
mite.config.growth_preview_saturated: The value reached the representable limit and is safely capped. In-game health is also subject to native attribute limits.
mite.config.growth_valid: Syntax, execution checks and current preview passed; ready to save
mite.config.growth_invalid: Formula validation failed; hover for the reason
mite.config.preview_fallback: The current preview triggered the runtime fallback. Adjust the formula or preview date before saving.
mite.config.invalid_preview_day: Preview day must be an integer of at least 1.
mite.config.invalid_growth_number: %s: enter a finite value from %s through %s.
mite.config.growth_reset.tooltip: Reset the health base, rates and formulas, and the fixed attack base. Applied only after Save.
mite.config.ore_generation.tooltip: Edit separate overworld and underworld generation multipliers. Default 1; enter 2, 0.5 or 0 to double, halve or disable. Original candidates and chance are read-only references.
mite.config.ore_deepslate_hint: This multiplier controls ores in deepslate; regular ores are configured separately. Both variants share the original candidate base, chance and height. Defaults do not add another vein batch.
mite.config.ore_multiplier_reset: Restore this mineral's multiplier and heights to the bundled factory preset for this dimension.
mite.config.ore_multiplier_invalid: %s invalid settings across both dimensions: multiplier 0–100; heights [minimum,maximum] with minimum <= maximum.
mite.config.ore_multiplier_hint: Multiplier: 1 original, 2 double, 0 disabled. Heights: [-100,100], new chunks only. Save applies both dimensions.
mite.config.ore_height_range.tooltip: Enter inclusive absolute Y coordinates, e.g. [-100,100]. Minimum must not exceed maximum; values -2032 to 2031 are clipped to the dimension's build limits. Regular and deepslate ores have independent ranges that constrain the entire vein. Restoring the default range preserves the original distribution.
mite.config.ore_surface_adamantium: Surface adamantium originally has zero candidates and remains disabled by default. Set advanced overworld_generation.adamantium.candidates above zero before its multiplier can affect generation.
mite.config.ore_underworld_modern_hint: Coal and emerald are modern underworld additions, absent from R196. Negative-height stone hosts deepslate variants; other stone hosts regular ore. Configure both variants independently.
mite.config.ore_candidates.tooltip: Candidate vein attempts before probability filtering in each new chunk. Range 0–100000; fractional attempts are probabilistic.
mite.config.ore_chance.tooltip: Chance for each candidate to proceed to a vein attempt, range 0–100. 0 disables generation; this is not the percentage of ore blocks.
mite.config.ore_actual_hint: Frequency means actual candidates per new chunk; pass chance is the only probability filter. Underworld counts are not multiplied by 8 again. Legacy *_frequency_* / *_chance_* keys correspond to these two fields; old JSON sample values are not imported. Default chance stays at 10%%; surface adamantium defaults to zero candidates. Terrain and vein size still affect placed blocks.
mite.config.ore_invalid: %s invalid entries across both dimensions: candidates must be 0–100000 and pass probability 0–100.
mite.config.spawning_rules.button.toolti: Edit natural monster caps, daily cap growth, spawn cooldown and pass probabilities.
mite.config.spawning_rules.title: Natural monster caps and timing
mite.config.spawning_rules.hint: Reference rules restore R196 caps, nearby crowd guards and timing. Saved numeric controls apply in custom mode only.
mite.config.spawning_rules.ite_hint: Adjust natural monster caps and timing together on this page. Save to apply immediately.
mite.config.spawning_rules.addon_hint: Spawn controls from the installed addon are loaded here. Every value can be edited; save to apply immediately.
mite.config.spawning_rules.reference_rul: Reference (default): R196 independent height caps, 8/10/12 nearby crowd guards and original timing; ignores custom numbers. Custom: restores the saved caps and timing below.
mite.config.spawning_rules.live: Save to apply immediately; no world reload needed
mite.config.spawning_rules.invalid: %s invalid values; check red fields on every page
mite.config.spawning_rules.reset.tooltip: Restore drafts on all pages to their defaults. Save to apply the changes.
mite.config.spawning_rules.base_cap.tool: Base monster count per 289 eligible spawn chunks. 0 removes the ordinary base allowance; daily growth is added separately. Existing mobs are retained.
mite.config.spawning_rules.blood_cap.too: Base monster count per 289 eligible chunks during blood moon dates. 0 removes the blood moon base allowance; daily growth is added separately.
mite.config.spawning_rules.daily_cap_inc: Extra monster allowance per day after day 1, per 289 eligible chunks, using the highest day ever reached in the overworld. Moving time backward does not lower the recorded highest day. 0 disables daily growth; decimals are supported.
mite.config.spawning_rules.maximum_cap.t: Upper bound on the base cap plus daily growth, per 289 eligible chunks. 0 means no additional upper bound.
mite.config.spawning_rules.hostile_inter: Minimum interval between hostile natural-spawn scheduling rounds. 20 ticks is about 1 second. 1 permits a round each tick; probability and placement checks still apply.
mite.config.spawning_rules.deep_chance_p: Base percentage chance for each scheduling round to attempt a deep hostile pass. 0 disables this band. Blood moon, dimension and dynamic rate modifiers still apply.
mite.config.spawning_rules.surface_chanc: Base percentage chance for each scheduling round to attempt a surface hostile pass. 0 disables this band. Actual spawning still requires terrain, light and population checks.
mite.config.spawning_rules.blood_chance_: Multiplier on hostile pass probability during blood moon dates; default 2. 0 disables hostile natural-spawn attempts on these dates. The final probability cannot exceed 100%.
mite.config.spawning_rules.dimension_cha: Hostile pass probability multiplier for the Nether, End and MITE underworld; default 0.25. 0 disables natural attempts in these dimensions; 1 uses the original base probability.
